pairs.question: Dic an corpus vegetet tractabile temet sive per aerias fallas, maledicte, figuras. Saltibus assuetus faunus mihi quippe videris.
pairs.answer: At si te propius venientem dextera nostra attingat, post Saxonibus memorare valebis, te nunc in Vosago fauni fantasma videre.
pairs.derivation: Ekivrid (line 760-763) genuinely asks whether Walther has a real tangible body or deceives through airy shapes: 'Dic an corpus vegetet tractabile temet / Sive per aerias fallas...'; the whole utterance, including the explanatory 'Saltibus assuetus faunus mihi quippe videris', is quoted contiguously as the question. Walther's reply (765-769, framed by 'dedit haec responsa') opens with a non-answering taunt about Ekivrid's people ('Celtica lingua probat te ex illa gente creatum, / Cui natura dedit reliquas ludendo praeire'), which is cut; the answer starts at the operative sentence 'At si te propius venientem dextera nostra / attingat...', which answers that he is corporeal (his real hand will strike). Stripped framing tag 'ait', speech quotes, and dangling verse numbers 765/770; no editorial angle brackets present.
